title: What if Mars's biggest volcano stood on Earth? 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
How high do you think you'd get before turning back? 👇

What if Olympus Mons, the biggest volcano in the solar system, stood on Earth? Climbing it would take you past Everest, past the Armstrong limit, and above NASA's highest-flying research jet.

Sources: NASA Science Photojournal, "Olympus Mons" (PIA25476, 2022); NASA JPL, "Olympus Mons" (PIA00300); Space.com, "Olympus Mons: The largest volcano in the solar system" (2023); NASA Armstrong (Dryden) ER-2 fact sheet FS-046; University of British Columbia ATSC 113, "Altitude and Pilot Physiology" (Armstrong limit).

scenes.text: You couldn't breathe on top of this volcano.
It's Olympus Mons on Mars, 25 kilometers tall and as wide as Arizona.
Put it on Earth and climb. Past Everest's 8,849 meters, the air is a third as thick.
At 19 kilometers, the saliva on your tongue starts to boil at body temperature.
At 21, you pass NASA's ER-2 jet, flying above 99 percent of the air.
The summit is still 4 kilometers higher. Only a pressure suit gets you there.
